items.title: Mozambique: Chapo meets Azura Power CEO Dave Peacock to discuss new energy sector investments
items.summary: The meeting provided an opportunity to discuss investment opportunities in the country’s energy sector and Azura Power’s interest in expanding its presence in Mozambique, at a time when the country is seeking to increase its power generation capacity and improve its energy infrastructure Azura Power is an Independent Power Producer (IPP) with a presence in several African markets, including Mozambique, where it is a co-owner of the Ressano Garcia Thermal Power Plant (CTRG), one of the largest privately owned power plants in operation in the country The company also operates in Nigeria and Senegal, carrying out activities related to power generation and supply and participating in energy infrastructure projects across the African continent Speaking after the meeting, Dave Peacock said the company intended to expand its presence in Mozambique across different areas of the energy sector “We are here today because we have great ambitions to do much more in Mozambique, both in power generation and in transmission and other related infrastructure,” said the Azura Power CEO Peacock said…

items.title: Hospitals deliberately targeted by Sudan's RSF fighters, BBC investigation finds
items.summary: Medics at el-Fasher's Saudi Hospital performed a Caesarean by phone light on the day it was bombed A BBC investigation has found evidence that Sudanese paramilitary fighters systematically destroyed el-Fasher's healthcare system during their long siege and subsequent takeover of the city in Darfur a year ago UN human rights chief Volker Türk called the findings "deeply disturbing", saying multiple attacks by the Rapid Support Forces (RSF) on civilian infrastructure, including health facilities, were serious violations of international humanitarian law and may amount to war crimes The RSF has rejected the BBC's findings The paramilitary group's health minister described the allegations as propaganda and a deliberate attempt by the national army and its allies to smear the RSF's reputation Using sources who were on the ground in el-Fasher, the BBC has found details of at least 43 separate attacks on hospitals and healthcare sites from May 2024 to October 2025 - some hit multiple times Under international law it is illegal to attack health facilities or their staff during conflict The…

items.title: Mozambique: Clear lines of financing for construction firms needed – president

items.title: Commercial banks sign agreements aimed at funding small businesses
items.summary: Maputo, 22 Oct (AIM) – Mozambican President Daniel Chapo has announced that six commercial banks have signed agreements to provide loans to small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) under the Mutual Guarantee Fund. The fund, now valued at 120 million US dollars, is designed to facilitate access to credit for businesses that lack sufficient assets to secure bank loans. With support from the World Bank, the government provides guarantees to banks and assumes part of the risk if beneficiary businesses default on their repayments. “We are talking about a fund that now stands at 120 million US dollars. We stress the importance of expanding financing opportunities for businesses led by women, which often face obstacles in accessing bank credit”, he said. Chapo said that his government was also reviewing legal instruments to facilitate the participation of domestic businesses, particularly those led by women, in the supply chains of major investment projects.

items.title: Surveillance and 'constant paranoia': Western diplomats tell BBC of life in war-time Moscow
items.summary: Ex-US and French ambassadors Lynne Tracy and Pierre Lévy were among those to speak to the BBC of their time in Moscow "Being the ambassador to Russia was probably the hardest assignment of my career," Lynne Tracy, who represented the US in Moscow from 2023 and 2025, tells the BBC US, UK and European diplomats once played a crucial role in Russia, defusing tensions even at the worst moments of the Cold War But now, deemed "unfriendly" by President Vladimir Putin's government, Western ambassadors are under constant surveillance, isolated and increasingly cut off from the country they were sent to understand, as the war in Ukraine grinds on through its fifth year The BBC has spoken to five diplomats who have served in Russia since it launched its full-scale invasion They compare current pressure levels to the Cold War era - when Western embassies were monitored through physical surveillance, listening devices hidden inside gifts , and "spy dust" - a near invisible chemical agent used to track officials Hundreds of Russian diplomats were expelled from countries in Europe and the US…

items.title: Lina Attalah: Mada Masr journalist sent for trial in Egypt
items.summary: Lina Attalah, who is accused of managing a website without a license, will go to court next week. items.title: Is Ebola under control in Kenya after nine cases confirmed?
items.summary: Nearly 5,000 healthcare workers have been trained to deal with Ebola Kenya is grappling with its first ever outbreak of Ebola, a disease which neighbouring countries, such as Uganda and Democratic Republic of Congo, are used to dealing with Nine cases have now been confirmed including its first patient, who travelled from DR Congo and died two weeks ago Four relatives of the first victim, three health workers and a hospital cleaner have now tested positive, meaning they are all linked to him But concerns are rising that the virus could start spreading further, even as the government has sought to assure citizens The US has warned it citizens against travelling to Kenya, while neighbouring countries such as Uganda, Ethiopia and Somalia are also on alert Kenyans have been expressing their concerns that the disease could spread more widely More than 4,000 people have died since Ebola was confirmed in DR Congo in May, making it the second most deadly outbreak of the disease With more than 9,500 cases in DR Congo, Kenya faces a steady risk of new cases arriving across borders, according…
